title: GTA VI’s jaw-dropping success: in figures
summary: Content creators have produced hundreds of millions of hours of video game since its launch Grand Theft Auto ( GTA) VI became the largest video game release of all time last week and while it is hard to say exactly how many people are playing the game (current estimates say at least 30 million), there are plenty of other jaw-dropping data points we do know. Data on streaming the game suggests that only two days into its release a cumulative 364.5m hours have been watched – roughly 41,000 years of content. Put another way, that translates to more than 41,000 years worth of people riffling through cash registers, hanging drywall, birding, diving or hijacking jets. That’s according to streaming data from Streams Charts, a data and analytics company that has been tracking Rockstar Game’s long-awaited title. Continue reading...

title: Man Theft Auto – why did so few women review GTA VI, the biggest video game of the decade?
summary: Given that this is the first Grand Theft Auto in 30 years with a female protagonist, you might have expected to hear from female critics. But you would have expected mostly in vain Grand Theft Auto VI is now the biggest video game launch of all time, and is likely to become the biggest video game of all time. It’s a once-in-a-lifetime event, a phenomenon that will shape games as a medium and pop culture at large for years to come, set against the backdrop of its developers fighting for their rights at studio Rockstar Games . It has snatched sales and streaming records and become the best-reviewed game ever (pulling ahead of 1998’s The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time). It’s also the first GTA game with a female protagonist, who also happens to be a woman of colour. Yet very few women (and seemingly no women of colour) played and reviewed it before release. When GTA VI’s review embargo lifted on 18 November, the gender imbalance was immediately obvious. Out of 156 reviewers, only six appeared to be women. As journalist Lex Luddy noted in a BlueSky post , that is 3.8%. Continue reading...

title: China’s Huawei convicted of stealing US trade secrets
summary: US attorney general Todd Blanche says ‘No person or company is above the law’ after tech giant found guilty on 10 of 12 criminal counts The Chinese telecommunications equipment maker Huawei was convicted on Tuesday in a sprawling US criminal case on charges that it stole ⁠trade secrets from US companies and deceived banks about ⁠its business in Iran. Huawei, the world’s leading telecom equipment manufacturer, was found guilty by a ​federal jury in Brooklyn of 10 of the 12 criminal counts it faced, including bank fraud, conspiracy to steal trade secrets and conspiracy to defraud the US. It was found not guilty of racketeering conspiracy, a charge alleging it had acted as a criminal enterprise. Continue reading...

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologizes to staff: ‘I made some terrible mistakes’
summary: Huang acknowledges he violated code of conduct by having affairs, but denied Trump was instrumental in his return Jensen Huang apologized to staff on Tuesday for the tumult he has caused at Nvidia. The company’s CEO acknowledged he violated the code of conduct for having extramarital affairs, but pushed back on the reports that Donald Trump was instrumental in his reinstatement as chief executive. “I made some terrible mistakes,” he said, according to a livestream reviewed by the New York Times . “I was unfaithful to Lori, and I hurt my kids and, of course, I hurt all of you.” Continue reading...

title: The Nvidia case is just the latest episode of Trump disregarding intelligence
summary: Trump’s reaction to sensitive information that contradicts his worldview mirrors his conduct towards war with Iran Donald Trump’s unwillingness to heed warnings of suspected Chinese penetration of the tech giant Nvidia follows a pattern of the US president ignoring sensitive intelligence that contradicts his world view. title: Trump, Nvidia and power: could we be nearing the end of tech’s Gilded Age?
summary: Oligarchs believe they’re untouchable – the blue wave offers hope that the rampant corruption of the Trump era may soon be over Nvidia staff: what do you think of Jensen Huang’s return as chief executive? One can imagine high-fives all around Nvidia’s boardroom after the board reinstated Jensen Huang to the CEO suite. The market gave the move a fat thumbs-up, boosting Nvidia’s share price by about a third. Shareholders, whose interests the board is meant to represent, are surely happy. But like Fifa’s controversial decision to defer the one-match suspension of US forward Folarin Balogun after receiving a red card for a foul on Bosnia and Herzegovina’s Tarik Muharemović during the World Cup over the summer, Huang’s absolution might backfire.
